steps.what: Review patient assessment, goals, preferences and relevant treatment constraints
outputs: verified treatment planning context and unresolved questions

steps.what: Develop the treatment plan with the patient and responsible professionals and record agreed actions
inputs: verified treatment planning context and unresolved questions
outputs: agreed treatment plan within professional authority

steps.what: Implement permitted treatment actions and coordinate the plan with the care team
inputs: agreed treatment plan within professional authority
outputs: implemented nursing actions and communicated treatment coordination needs

tasks.design: Retain treatment development and implementation with the appropriately authorised psychiatric nurse and care team using the existing clinical record {OTHER}. No model chooses treatment or converts a draft into a clinical commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan depends on patient context, preferences, clinical judgement and practical delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records support planning without a new model.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve conflicting goals, uncertainty and barriers to implementation.
tasks.human_edge: Build a shared plan that fits the patient and recognise limits of professional authority.

reach.task: Resolve treatment choices beyond nursing authority
reach.learn: Which patient concerns or constraints change the plan

evidence.claim: Clinical documentation drafting does not establish that psychiatric treatment choice or implementation takes less time.

assumptions: The nurse verifies actual professional scope; the occupational title alone does not grant prescribing or independent treatment authority.
Existing clinicians produce source assessments; the nurse verifies planning context in s1, captures agreed actions in s2 and implements permitted actions in s3, with all time retained.
No free structured patient preference, generated diagnosis or clean treatment-option feed is assumed.
This task overlaps interdisciplinary planning in practice; no additive saving or new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Local treatment authority and planning process
research_questions: Which treatment decisions require separate clinician authorisation in this setting?

already_counted.description: Context review, plan development and implementation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new treatment system or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work give zero saving. No invented plan-transcription baseline or reduced clinical delivery time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in professional development and continuing education

steps.what: Identify professional learning needs and choose suitable conferences or continuing education activities
Participate in conferences or continuing education and reflect on learning relevant to psychiatric nursing

tasks.design: Retain activity selection, participation and reflection using existing learning tools {LMS}, activity listings {OTHER} and learning notes {DOCS}. No generated attendance evidence or shortcut through actual learning is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful development requires selecting relevant learning and actively engaging with it.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning and conference resources support this unchanged task.
tasks.still_hard: Judge relevance and relate new knowledge critically to practice.
tasks.human_edge: Reflect on experience and question what the learning means for patient care.
tasks.altitude: Meaningful professional development remains the work.

reach.task: Clarify relevant learning opportunities and evidence
reach.learn: Which activities address actual practice questions

evidence.claim: A documentation tool does not demonstrate reduced participation or reflective learning time.

assumptions: The nurse produces learning questions in s1; education providers produce activity details and materials through existing work.
All selection, registration clarification, attendance, reflection and participation evidence capture remain in s1-s2.
No free structured learning need or competence score is assumed.
Existing registration and learning tools are already in the baseline; no new alert system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current professional requirements and activity choices
research_questions: Which activities best answer the nurse's actual practice learning questions?

already_counted.description: Selection, participation and reflection remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new learning service or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero saving. No unestablished enrolment burden or shortened learning is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with the psychiatric interdisciplinary team on treatment plans

steps.what: Prepare relevant nursing observations and unresolved treatment questions for interdisciplinary discussion
outputs: verified nursing contribution and planning questions

steps.what: Collaborate with psychiatrists, psychologists and nursing staff to develop, implement or evaluate treatment plans
inputs: verified nursing contribution and planning questions
outputs: shared treatment evaluation and agreed responsibilities

tasks.design: Retain interdisciplinary collaboration using current clinical records {OTHER}. No synthetic team consensus or generated treatment evaluation replaces professional discussion and agreement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical views and practical treatment responsibilities must be reconciled among people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and meeting channels support the work without a new model.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve disagreement and interpret response in a complex patient context.
tasks.human_edge: Bring direct nursing observations and challenge incomplete assumptions.
tasks.altitude: Clear shared treatment understanding and responsibilities.

reach.task: Clarify treatment assumptions and evaluation concerns
reach.learn: Which nursing observations affect the shared approach

evidence.claim: Clinical note drafting does not establish reduced interdisciplinary treatment discussion time.

assumptions: Care staff produce current records and observations through existing care; preparation and question capture remain fully retained in s1.
All team discussion and agreement capture remain in s2; no free structured consensus or evaluation feed is assumed.
This task overlaps the broader treatment-plan task and is not additive.
Other professionals' labour remains unchanged outside focal savings; no new collaboration system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Team roles and current collaboration process
research_questions: Which treatment assumptions most often require reconciliation between disciplines?

already_counted.description: Preparation and interdisciplinary collaboration remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new collaboration service or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work yield zero saving. No team conversation or evaluation time is reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult specialists about unusual or complex cases

steps.what: Identify unusual or complex case concerns and verify the information needed for specialist consultation
outputs: verified consultation question and supporting case context

steps.what: Consult psychiatrists or other professionals on complex cases and clarify advice and follow-up responsibilities
inputs: verified consultation question and supporting case context
outputs: documented consultation understanding and follow-up responsibilities

tasks.design: Retain preparation and direct specialist consultation using existing clinical records {OTHER}. No general model supplies specialist advice or replaces clarification of complex case uncertainty.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficult part is understanding the case and obtaining appropriate professional judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and consultation channels support the work without a new agent.
tasks.still_hard: Communicate uncertainty and establish what the advice means for this patient.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise limits and ask the specialist the right follow-up question.
tasks.altitude: Useful specialist consultation with clear ownership of follow-up.

reach.task: Clarify complex case questions and follow-up

evidence.claim: Clinical documentation tools do not establish reduced specialist reasoning or consultation time for complex cases.

assumptions: The nurse identifies and verifies the question in s1; all source review and preparation remain counted.
The specialist produces advice through consultation in s2, where nurse clarification and recording time remain fully retained.
No free specialist opinion, structured complexity code or newly reconciled case summary is assumed.
Specialist labour is unchanged outside the focal baseline; no new consultation model or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current specialist access and consultation process
research_questions: Which case context is most often missing when a consultation begins?

already_counted.description: Case preparation and specialist consultation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new consultation tool or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero saving. No invented administration or shortened complex-case reasoning.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve patient-specific treatment judgement, interdisciplinary collaboration and specialist consultation.
reach: Clarify treatment assumptions with psychiatrists and psychologists
Choose relevant development with education staff
role.ambitious_version: A psychiatric nurse who brings clear evidence and patient understanding to accountable team decisions.
